source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Anthracnose is a fungal disease affecting leaves, twigs, flowers, and fruit, caused by a fungus that produces spores in small fruiting bodies on infected tissue, especially dead or stressed wood. On leaves it can cause spotting and blighting; on twigs it contributes to dieback; and on fruit it can cause dark, sunken lesions, particularly on fruit that is already stressed, wounded, or over-mature.

Infection is favored by warm, humid, rainy conditions, which help spores spread by rain-splash from infected plant material onto healthy new growth and developing fruit; trees that are otherwise weakened by drought, poor nutrition, or other stress are typically more severely affected.

Control includes pruning out and destroying infected and dead wood to reduce the spore source, ensuring good tree nutrition and irrigation to reduce plant stress, and applying protective copper-based fungicide sprays during wet periods when new growth and fruit are most vulnerable to infection.
